requirement: Load a JWKS document, keep only its signing keys indexed by kid, and verify RS256 tokens for an audience with exactly the key their kid names.
skeleton: A JwksVerifier class whose constructor filters PyJWKSet keys by kid and use and refuses an empty result, and whose verify looks up the kid strictly and decodes with RS256 and the audience.
caption: JWKS-based JWT verification with PyJWT. JwksVerifier(jwks, audience) parses the document with jwt.PyJWKSet.from_dict and indexes by key_id only the keys that have a kid and whose public_key_use is sig or unset, so encryption keys are left out; it raises ValueError saying the JWKS contains no signing keys with a kid when nothing remains. verify(token) reads the kid with jwt.get_unverified_header; a missing, non-string or unlisted kid raises jwt.InvalidTokenError saying there is no signing key for that kid repr, never falling back to another key. It then decodes with that key, algorithms pinned to RS256 and the configured audience, so a kid pointing at another key raises jwt.InvalidSignatureError and a wrong aud raises jwt.InvalidAudienceError. The fixture asserts that kids a and b each verify their own tokens, that a token signed by a but labelled b raises jwt.InvalidSignatureError, that kid zz and a missing kid raise jwt.InvalidTokenError naming 'zz' and None, that the enc key raises jwt.InvalidTokenError naming 'enc', that audience admin raises jwt.InvalidAudienceError, and that a JWKS with only an enc key raises ValueError.

plan.intent: Verify tokens from an identity provider's published keys
constraints: Only keys with a kid and use sig or no use are indexed
A JWKS with no such keys raises ValueError
Missing or unknown kids raise jwt.InvalidTokenError without falling back to another key
A kid naming the wrong key raises jwt.InvalidSignatureError
Tokens are decoded with RS256 only and the configured audience, a wrong aud raises jwt.InvalidAudienceError

rationale.teaches: Use PyJWKSet to parse the document, filter by use, and treat an unknown kid as an invalid token rather than guessing a key.
rationale.why: Falling back to the first key or accepting encryption keys quietly widens what can sign, and a KeyError on an unknown kid turns a bad token into a server error.

ops.docstring: Verify RS256 tokens against the signing key a JWKS document lists for their kid.

candidates.why_wrong: Keys marked for encryption are indexed and accepted as signing keys.
No audience is passed, so every token with an aud claim is rejected.
Tokens without a known kid fall back to the first key instead of being rejected.
A JWKS without signing keys is accepted and every later token is refused.
An unknown kid raises KeyError instead of a JWT error the caller can map to 401.
